State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Punjab National Bank vs Pradeep Kumar Gairola on 28 August, 2024
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
 159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola

STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION UTTARAKHAND, DEHRADUN

 Date of Admission : 29.11.2021
 Date of Final Hearing : 02.08.2024
 Date of Pronouncement : 28.08.2024

 First Appeal No. 159 / 2021

1. Punjab National Bank
 A Corporate Body, Branch Race Course, Dehradun
 Through its Chief Manager Sh. Pradeep Singhal

2. Punjab National Bank
 A Corporate Body, 7 PNB House, Bhikaji Cama Place
 Africa Avenue, New Delhi
 Through Branch Race Course, Dehradun
 Through its Chief Manager Sh. Pradeep Singhal
 (Through: Sh. S.M. Joshi, Advocate)
 .....Appellants

 VERSUS

Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola S/o Late Sh. Dwarika Prasad Gairola
R/o 51-3/2, Haridwar Road, Dehradun
 ..... Respondent in Person

Coram:
Ms. Kumkum Rani, President
Mr. B.S. Manral, Member

 ORDER
(Per: Ms. Kumkum Rani, President):
This appeal under
Section 15
of The Consumer Protection Act, 1986
has been directed against judgment and order dated 16.10.2021 passed by
the learned District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Dehradun
(hereinafter to be referred as the District Commission) in consumer
1
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
 159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola

complaint No. 236 of 2015 styled as
Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola Vs. Punjab
National Bank and Anr.
, wherein and whereby the complaint was allowed.
2. The facts giving rise to the appeal, in brief, are as such that the
complainant, a senior citizen, is an account holder (Account No.
1532000300000114) with the opposite party No. 1 since 29.04.2005 and
also holds its ATM card bearing No. 5126520133930870. The complainant
has withdrawn an amount of Rs. 15,000/- on 20th April, 2015 through ATM
machine kept in the premises of opposite party No. 1 using his ATM card
issued by the opposite party No. 1. All along the ATM card was in the
possession of the complainant under safe custody under lock and key
beyond the reach of anyone. Also the information regarding the said ATM
card was neither shared with anyone telephonically, verbally nor through
e-mails nor made any purchases through ATM card in last many years. The
complainant was amazed to learn on getting his pass-book updated on dated
12.05.2015 that there has been unauthorized and fraudulent withdrawal
from his account between 28.04.2015 and 07.05.2015 through the ATMs
till the balance of Rs. 463.35 was left. The pass-book entry reveals that the
withdrawals on six days, i.e. 29.04.2015, 30.04.2015, 01.05.2015,
04.05.2015, 05.05.2015 & 06.05.2015 were to the tune of Rs. 25,000/- on
each day made through as many as three to four transactions and on dated
28.04.2015 and 04.05.2015 Rs. 50,120/- were withdrawn through six
transactions on each day and finally Rs. 9,020/- was withdrawn on dated
07.05.2015. Thus, a total amount of Rs. 2,59,600/- was fraudulently
withdrawn from his account. This fact was immediately brought to the
notice of the opposite party No. 1, who in turn advised the complainant to
get the said ATM card blocked and get FIR registered with the police and
assured him to do the needful from their side. The complainant immediately
got the said ATM card blocked and informed the police in writing. Again
2
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
 159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola

the second written complaint was made with the police on dated
13.05.2015. On account of not getting FIR till 18.05.2015, a formal written
complaint was made with the opposite party No. 1 on dated 18.05.2015
alongwith copies of the written complaint to the police and the relevant
extract of passbook showing the unauthorized withdrawals. The opposite
party No. 1 once again assured the complainant that they will do their best
to help him out. The opposite party No. 1 has neither responded to
complainant's letter and nor had given back the money. On the contrary,
the complainant was made to run many times for enquiries on the progress
of the matter, but without any results. The conduct of the opposite parties
amounts to deficiency in service of providing a secure and reliable banking
and on account of the defiant attitude of the opposite parties, the
complainant has suffered mental agony, therefore, the complainant has
sought relief from the opposite parties to refunds Rs. 2,59,600/- alongwith
interest @ 24% per annum on the said amount with compensation of Rs.
1,00,000/- for harassment and mental agony with litigation charges.
3. The opposite parties have jointly submitted their written statement
wherein it is alleged that the complainant has committed negligence and
has not noted while making transactions through his ATM card and has not
kept the said ATM card in safe custody. The complainant has shared the
security pin code and secret information with someone. It is further pleaded
in the written statement that the transactions were made with his ATM card
through various banks, which has clarified that there was gross negligence
on the part of the complainant. It is further submitted that the transactions
through the said ATM card could not be made without sharing ATM card
alongwith pin number to someone else. There is possibility that a servant
or family members of the account holder has taken the card in question and
withdrawn the money through the said ATM card from the account of the
3
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
 159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola

complainant, for which the complainant himself is responsible and for such
fraudulent transactions, the Bank is not anywhere responsible. The
complainant has not averred that there was any connection of the
employees of the Bank because the FIR was against unknown person.
There is no deficiency in service on the part of the answering opposite
parties and the alleged transactions were made due to the negligence of
account holder for which the answering opposite parties are not
responsible. Hence, in such circumstances, the complaint is liable to be
dismissed.
4. The District Commission after hearing both the parties and after
taking into consideration the pleadings and evidence available on record,
passed the impugned judgment and order on dated 16.10.2021 allowing the
complaint case and directing the opposite parties to pay Rs. 2,59,600/- to
the complainant alongwith Rs. 25,000/- for mental agony and Rs. 10,000/-
towards costs of litigation within 30 days, failing which the complainant
shall be entitled to get simple interest @ 9% per annum from the date of
filing of the complaint till its actual realization.
5. Aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order of the District
Commission, the opposite parties have preferred the present appeal as
appellants.
6. Learned counsel for the appellants has contended that the impugned
judgment and order is against law and facts of the case. The Commission
below has committed error in believing the allegations and version of the
respondent. The matter was regarding the withdrawal of amount using
respondent's ATM card and it was used in Delhi and other places of
different Bank, but those were not made parties in the complaint case. RBI
4
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
 159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola

has not made SMS facility compulsory, it was optional and the respondent
was not availing the same during the alleged transactions period. But the
Commission below has given its finding contrary to this, hence the
impugned judgment and order is perverse. The respondent must negligently
have shared PIN number, CVC number, Pass-word and OTP to someone,
then the alleged fraud is possible, therefore, the appellants are not liable to
reimburse the same. The respondent is very old person and he may engage
any of his close relative or grand children to withdraw the money from
ATM and such person may misuse the ATM card. In case of fraud, the
consumer complaint is not maintainable, because it requires voluminous
evidence. In the present complaint, the respondent intimated the appellants
after last transaction, so the respondent is liable for the same. The appellants
had not committed any negligence, therefore, the appeal may kindly be
allowed and the impugned judgment and order be set aside.
7. We have heard learned counsel for the appellants as well as
respondent in person and perused the material available on record.
8. It is an admitted fact that the respondent - complainant is a senior
citizen, who holds a bank account No. 1532000300000114 since
29.04.2005 in the opposite parties' bank. It is also proved on record that the
appellants had issued an ATM card No. 5126520133930870 to the
respondent. It is also not disputed that the respondent had withdrawn Rs.
15,000/- through ATM card from his account on dated 20.04.2015. It is
contended on behalf of the appellants that the Commission below has
committed error in believing the allegations and version of the respondent.
The complaint was regarding withdrawal of amount using respondent's
ATM card and it was used in Delhi and other places of different bank, but
5
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
 159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola

those banks were not made parties in the complaint case, hence the
complaint was not maintainable.
9. We are not agreed with such contention because in the written
statement, filed in the Commission below the appellants had pleaded in para
No. 23 that withdrawals through ATM card were made through various
banks, but in the written statement, the appellants' Bank has not stated that
the withdrawal through ATM card of the respondent was made and used in
Delhi and other places in the different banks. In the absence of such clear
contention, the respondent cannot be held guilty for not impleading the
other various banks as necessary party in the complaint case. Apart from
it, the respondent is the account holder of the appellants Bank and ATM
card was also issued from the appellants Bank. As per the version of the
appellants, if the transactions were made from various banks, then in such
circumstances the appellants should clarify about the status of the
withdrawal on the alleged date from those banks and also submit relevant
evidence in this regard, but such relevant evidence of the various banks was
not submitted by the appellants, hence it could not be said that the various
banks were not made party in the complaint case and the complaint is bad
for non-joinder of necessary parties. It is also argued on behalf of the
appellants that the alleged withdrawals were made during 28.04.2015 to
07.05.2015 and RBI has not made SMS facility compulsory it was optional
and the respondent was not availing this facility during the above period,
so the finding of the Commission below is contrary to this fact, hence the
impugned judgment is perverse.
10. Respondent has alleged that he has submitted the literature regarding
this on the record of the appeal.
6
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
 159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola
11. As per the literature regarding the alert services, the bank issued
important information that the debit / credit card transaction alerts sent as
per regulatory guidelines and internet banking transaction alerts do not
form part of SMS banking service. Customers who are not registered for
chargeable SMS banking service will continue to get these alerts free of
charge (paper No. 51 of the appeal record).
12. Vide letter of RBI dated 29.03.2011 (paper No. 44), the Reserve
Bank of India had issued some guidelines and a letter to this fact was sent
to the Chairman and Managing Director / Chief Executive Officers to take
steps to put in place a system of online alerts for all types of transactions
irrespective of the amount, involving usage of cards at various channels.
As the Banks were directed to implement this measure latest by June, 30
2011. So, as per the literature, it is mandatory on the part of the bank to
give SMS alert facility while the transaction through debit / credit card was
made. The appellants plea is that the charges for SMS alert were not paid
by the respondent, hence such facility was not given, but as per guidelines
of RBI, any transaction made through debit / credit card, such SMS alert
facility should be given without any charges or free of charge. Thus, on
such count, there was negligence on the part of the appellants not taking
appropriate security measures, online alerts to the card-holders at the use of
debit / credit card.
13. It is also established on record that the respondent has lodged a police
report under Crime No. NlL/15 under
Section 420
IPC. As per evidence
available on record, it is evident that in the ATM at Race Course, neither
there was security guard in the premises, nor there was any CCTV camera in
other ATM centers of Punjab National Bank in Dehradun. As per guidelines
of RBI, a CCTV Camera should be installed inside the ATM centers.
7
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
 159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola
14. The appellants have failed to prove that the ATM centers, where the
alleged transactions were illegally and fraudulently made, have security
guard. It is also proved on record that CCTV camera footage has not been
submitted in evidence to prove that unmanned ATM centers in isolated
areas have the CCTV camera footage to record such incidents. As the
process to fix skimmers requires at least half an hour, it cannot be done, if
the center is guarded. Appellants have not submitted any evidence
regarding the fact that the security camera was properly installed in the
ATM centers wherefrom fraudulent transactions were made. It usually
happens that the skimmers and the gang opted four ATMs because these
facilities had neither a security guard, nor a CCTV camera.
15. We have also perused the guidelines of RBI through the notification
Nos. RBI/2013-14/296 dated 27.09.2013 and RBI/2017-18/15 dated
06.07.2017. In the above guidelines dated 06.07.2017, it is mentioned in
para Nos. 3, 4 & 5.
"3. Broadly, the electronic banking transactions can be
 divided into two categories:
i. Remote/ online payment transactions (transactions
 that do not require physical payment instruments to
 be presented at the point of transactions e.g. internet
 banking, mobile banking, card not present (CNP)
 transactions), Pre-paid Payment Instruments (PPI),
 and
 ii. Face-to-face/ proximity payment transactions
 (transactions which require the physical payment
 instrument such as a card or mobile phone to be
 present at the point of transaction e.g. ATM, POS,
 etc.)
8
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola
4. The systems and procedures in banks must be
 designed to make customers feel safe about carrying out
 electronic banking transactions. To achieve this, banks
 must put in place:
i. appropriate systems and procedures to ensure safety
 and security of electronic banking transactions
 carried out by customers;
ii. robust and dynamic fraud detection and prevention
 mechanism;
iii. mechanism to assess the risks (for example, gaps in
 the bank's existing systems) resulting from
 unauthorised transactions and measure the
 liabilities arising out of such events;
 iv. appropriate measures to mitigate the risks and
protect themselves against the liabilities arising
 therefrom; and
 v. a system of continually and repeatedly advising
 customers on how to protect themselves from
 electronic banking and payments related fraud.
Reporting of unauthorised transactions by
 customers to banks.
5. Banks must ask their customers to mandatorily
 register for SMS alerts and wherever available register for
 e-mail alerts, for electronic banking transactions. The
 SMS alerts shall mandatorily be sent to the customers,
 while email alerts may be sent, wherever registered. The
 customers must be advised to notify their bank of any
 unauthorised electronic banking transaction at the earliest
 after the occurrence of such transaction, and informed that
9
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola

 the longer the time taken to notify the bank, the higher will
 be the risk of loss to the bank/ customer. To facilitate this,
 banks must provide customers with 24x7 access through
 multiple channels (at a minimum, via website, phone
 banking, SMS, e-mail, IVR, a dedicated toll-free helpline,
 reporting to home branch, etc.) for reporting unauthorised
 transactions that have taken place and/ or loss or theft of
 payment instrument such as card, etc. Banks shall also
 enable customers to instantly respond by "Reply" to the
 SMS and e-mail alerts and the customers should not be
 required to search for a web page or an e-mail address to
 notify the objection, if any. Further, a direct link for
 lodging the complaints, with specific option to report
 unauthorised electronic transactions shall be provided by
 banks on home page of their website. The loss/ fraud
 reporting system shall also ensure that immediate response
 (including auto response) is sent to the customers
 acknowledging the complaint along with the registered
 complaint number. The communication systems used by
 banks to send alerts and receive their responses thereto
 must record the time and date of delivery of the message
 and receipt of customer's response, if any, to them. This
 shall be important in determining the extent of a
 customer's liability. The banks may not offer facility of
 electronic transactions, other than ATM cash withdrawals,
 to customers who do not provide mobile numbers to the
 bank. On receipt of report of an unauthorised transaction
 from the customer, banks must take immediate steps to
 prevent further unauthorised transactions in the account."
10
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
 159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola
16. From the record, it is also evident that the fraudulent and illegal
transactions were made through various banks, i.e. from Delhi & other
places. Respondent has clearly averred in the affidavit and evidence that
he never intimated his particulars, pin-code of the card and personal
information to any other person to make the illegal transactions.
17. It is also evident on record that after receiving the information about
such illegal transactions, the respondent immediately got his card blocked
after contacting the Bank and also lodged a complaint about such incident
to the P.S. Dalanwala, Dehradun on dated 30.05.2015.
18. All the above facts have revealed that the respondent was having a
debit card in his saving account. If the information about the card password
was shared by the respondent to some other person, then he would neither
lodge the FIR nor he would get his card blocked from the Bank. Thus, it is
proved that the respondent had taken all the necessary steps which were
required to be taken after getting knowledge of illegal transaction.
19. In the guidelines RBI/2013-14/296 dated 27.09.2013, reference is
mentioned regarding the circular No. DPSS PD CO. No.
513/02.14.003/2011-2012 dated September 22, 2011 on security issues
and risk mitigation measures related to Card Present (CP) transactions and
circulars DPSS (CO) PD No. 1462/2377/02.14.003/2012-13 dated
February 28, 2013 and June 24, 2013 respectively on security and risk
mitigation measures for electronic payment transactions, wherein various
timelines were indicated for compliance. But several banks had
approached for seeking further extension of the time line of September 30,
2013 for complying with the task of securing the technology infrastructure.
11
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
 159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola

But the RBI had decided not to grant any further extension of time and
ordered the following course of action is mandated:-
a. The issuing bank would ascertain, within 3
 working days from the date of cardholder
 approaching the bank, whether the respective POS
 terminal/s where the said transaction/s occurred
 is/are compliant with TLE and UKPT/DUKPT as
 mandated.
b. In the event it is found that the POS terminals are
 non-compliant as mandated, the issuing bank shall
 pay the disputed amount to the customer within 7
 working days, failing which a compensation of
 Rs.100 per day will be payable to the customer from
 the 8th working day.
c. The issuing bank shall claim the amount paid by
 it to the customer from the respective bank/s which
 have acquired the POS transaction/s in question.
d. The acquiring banks have to pay the amount paid
 by the issuing bank without demur within 3 working
 days of the issuing bank raising the claim, failing
 which the Reserve Bank of India would be
 constrained to compensate the issuing bank by
 debiting the account of the acquiring bank
 maintained with the Bank.
20. Thus, as per the guidelines mentioned in the above said
notifications, if the issuing banks had not taken action upon receiving the
12
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
 159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola

complaint about illegal and fraudulent transactions of card holder, then the
issuing bank shall pay the disputed amount to the customers.
21. In the present case, the respondent has made the intimation to the
Bank immediately about the fraudulent and illegal transactions to the tune
of Rs. 2,59,600/-, but the appellant Bank did not take any action.
22. If the illegal and fraudulent transactions were made without sharing
pin-code CVV value and password to any other person, even then the
transactions have taken place from different places, in such circumstances,
it will be deemed that there was no negligence on the part of the respondent
- complainant and such transactions took place due to the reason that the
Bank had not provided sufficient proof security for the card transaction.
23. Learned counsel for the appellant has referred the following case
laws, which are as follows:
1.
Revision Petition No. 2082 of 2017, Praveen
 Kumar Jain Vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.
decided on
 28.12.2023 (Hon'ble National Commission)
2.
Revision Petition No. 3073 of 2016, State Bank
 of India vs. Dr. J.C.S. Kataky
, decided on
 03.05.2017 (Hon'ble National Commission)
3.
First Appeal No. 112 of 2015, Chairman
 Punjab National Bank & Anr. vs. Leader Valves
 Ltd.
, decided on 13.03.2020 (Hon'ble National
 Commission)
13
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
 159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola
4.
Revision Petition No. 3333 of 2013, HDFC
 Bank Limited and another vs. Jesna Jose
,
 decided on 21.12.2020 (Hon'ble National
 Commission)
24.
In the case of
Parveen Kumar Jain vs. HDFC Bank Ltd.
(supra),
the Hon'ble National Commission has held that "as per these instructions,
there will be zero liability of a customer, where the unauthorized
transaction occurs in the events of Contributory fraud/ deficiency on the
part of the bank. The instructions also take care of third party breach where
the deficiency lies neither with the bank nor with the customer but lies
elsewhere in the system. If customer notifies the Bank of such transaction
within three working days, then zero liability lies with the customer."
In
the above case
, the Hon'ble National Commission has set aside
the order so the State Commission as well as District Commission and
allow the complaint with the directions to the respondent - HDFC Bank to
reverse the transactions with respect to the fraudulent transactions which
took place on dated 30.03.2014 for a total amount of Rs. 24,000/-. In case
this amount has already been recovered from the complainant, the Bank is
liable to refund the same alongwith interest / penalty charged on such
amount and such refund shall be payable to the complainant alongwith
interest with litigation charges.
In the instant case, the respondent - complainant had paid the
amount of illegal transaction alongwith charges, so the above said case is
fully applicable to the case in hand.
25.
In the case of
State Bank of India vs. Dr. J.C.S. Kataky
(supra),
the Hon'ble National Commission has held that "A plain reading of this
provision is sufficient to establish that once the complaint was made citing
14
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
 159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola

specific incidents of unauthorised withdrawal, it was the duty of the Bank
to have carried out the necessary verification in the matter, rather than
washing their hands off from the whole episode. Evidently, there has been
deficiency in service on the part of the Bank, vis-à-vis, the
consumer/complainant. It is held, therefore, that the consumer fora below
have made a correct appreciation of the facts and circumstances on record
which deciding the complaint in favour of the complainant. Moreover, it
is a settled legal proposition that the powers in the exercise of the revisional
jurisdiction are used only if there is a jurisdictional error or material defect
in the orders passed by the consumer fora". Therefore, on such discussion,
the Hon'ble National Commission dismissed the revision petition on merit.
26.
In the case of
Chairman, Punjab National Bank & Anr. vs.
Leader Valves Ltd.
(supra), the Hon'ble National Commission has held
that "it is seen that the Complainant, on his part, had been diligent and
dutiful in bringing the unauthorized transfers to the notice of the Bank
without undue delay, he brought the unauthorized transactions to the
Bank's notice the same day, in the evening, on checking his accounts. His
responsibility ended there, and the Bank's responsibility started, it was the
Bank's responsibility to identify the systemic failure, remedy the pecuniary
loss and injury to the Complainant."
In the abovesaid case, the Hon'ble National Commission has also
confirmed the order of the State Commission wherein the award was made
in favour of the complainant.
27.
In the case of
HDFC Bank Limited and another vs. Jesna Jose
(supra), the Hon'ble National Commission has held that "The first
fundamental question that arises is whether the Bank is responsible for an
unauthorized transfer occasioned by an act of malfeasance on the part of
15
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
 159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola

functionaries of the Bank or by an act of malfeasance by any other person
(except the Complainant / account-holder). The answer, straightaway, is in
the affirmative. If an account is maintained by the Bank, the Bank itself is
responsible for its safety and security. Any systemic failure, whether by
malfeasance on the part of its functionaries or by any other person (except
the consumer / account-holder), is its responsibility, and not of the
consumer." and dismissed the revision and confirmed the order of the State
Commission as well as the District Commission.
28. So in the light of the above cited case laws, it is proved that there
was no negligence on the part of the respondent and he had immediately
intimated about the occurrence / illegal transactions made from his card to
the Bank, but nothing was done by the Bank. The illegal transactions were
made from different banks. It is not proved on record that the respondent
had shared the CVV value, pin-code, password and personal information
of his card to someone else.
29. The appellant had not filed any such cogent evidence to this effect
that the respondent was negligent and he has shared his confidential
information about his card to someone else, therefore, we find no
negligence or carelessness on the part of the respondent.
30. We are of the considered view that the District Commission has not
committed any error in awarding the sum of Rs. 2,59,600/- alongwith
Rs. 25,000/- towards mental agony and Rs. 10,000/- for litigation charges
to the respondent. Thus, we are of the considered view that the District
Commission has exercised the jurisdiction which was vested in it and the
impugned judgment is perfectly and appropriately passed by the District
Commission concerned. There is no perversity and infirmity in passing of
16
Appeal No. Punjab National Bank & Anr. 28.08.2024
 159 of 2021 Vs.
 Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gairola

the impugned judgment. Thus, the impugned judgment deserves to be
affirmed and the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
31. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed. Impugned judgment and
order dated 16.10.2021 passed by the District Commission, Dehradun is
hereby affirmed. No order as to costs of the appeal.
32. A copy of this Order be provided to all the parties free of cost as
mandated by the
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
/ 2019. The Order be
uploaded forthwith on the website of the Commission for the perusal of
the parties. The copy of this Order be sent to the concerned District
Commission for record and necessary information.
33. File be consigned to record room along with a copy of this Order.
(Ms. Kumkum Rani)
 President

 (Mr. B.S. Manral)
 Member
Pronounced on: 28.08.2024
17
